node.label: Eugene Genovese
node.date_label: The Political Economy of Slavery (1965) · Roll, Jordan, Roll (1974) · From Rebellion to Revolution (1979)
node.description: A historian of slavery in the American South whose work joins economic structures, culture and domination. Roll, Jordan, Roll interprets paternalism as a contested relationship of power, not benign treatment. The primary preface and opening retain their own national-culture framing; Walter Johnson’s later review challenges the account’s implications for consent and coercion. A separate reading by N. Gordon Levin discusses the earlier political-economy argument and its problems, preserving the distinction between a named reader’s criticism and Genovese’s own text.
node.representative_figures_and_works: The Political Economy of Slavery (1965; later editions distinct); Roll, Jordan, Roll (1974; preface dated August 1973, Vintage 1976 distinct); From Rebellion to Revolution (1979; 1981 reprint distinct).
node.scope_note: Existing primary preface/opening and named Johnson reading retain all qualifications. Earlier/later political identities do not collapse the writings into one timeless position. Levin is a named substantive reader, not Genovese’s own statement. No direct Gramsci passage has been checked, and acknowledgments do not establish agreement or coauthorship.

proposed_edges.relationship: Interprets enslaved culture and paternalism as contested forms within a system of domination.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Existing complete preface and initial paternalism paragraphs, plus Walter Johnson’s complete retrospective, within their recorded scopes. Paternalism is not a benign-slavery claim; Johnson’s consent/coercion criticism remains visible.

proposed_edges.relationship: Makes the relation between slaveholding class power, economic organization and development a problem for Marxist historical interpretation.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Specific political-economy intervention mediated by N. Gordon Levin’s substantive review, selected opening pages. This is a contribution to a contested interpretation, not proof that every Marxist shared it, or a direct personal influence from Marx or Gramsci.
